prompt: What really caused the 2008 financial crisis? Tell it as a story starting from the US housing boom, include subprime mortgages, securitization, Lehman Brothers and the government response.

plan.title: What Really Caused the 2008 Financial Crisis
plan.description: The 2008 financial crisis began with a US housing boom, risky subprime mortgages and securitization, then peaked with Lehman Brothers' collapse. Here is the story in 30 seconds, including the government response.

beats.narration: Banks handed mortgages to people who couldn't repay them, then sold those loans as safe investments. That's how the world broke.

props.alt: row of homes in a neighborhood

beats.narration: Housing boomed. Subprime loans spread, and banks bundled them into securities rated safe. When prices fell, borrowers defaulted and those securities collapsed.
In September 2008, Lehman Brothers went bankrupt. Markets crashed worldwide.
Government stepped in with bailouts like TARP. Lesson: when everyone ignores the risk, everyone pays.

props.text: When everyone ignores the risk, everyone pays.

warnings: length: the narration totals 68 words in 4 beats but a 30-second video needs about 58 (between 52 and 58). Cut about 10 words: 3 to 4 beats of about 19 words each (you averaged 17; count the words of every beat), one idea, no preamble and no recap; keep the hook and the last line
